title: Waiver Watch List
brief: Which undrafted players should we watch in the first weeks for role, minutes or starting changes that make them worth a FAB bid? Each line must state the trigger that would make us add him.
summary: The first two weeks after our 2026-10-18 auction are when coaches surprise people, so check opening-night starting lineups, minutes and injuries daily and bid FAB quickly when a player gets a real starting role. A new starting job is worth a real bid and a longer hold. A fill-in start during a short injury is a short-term add, so bid small and plan to drop him when the starter returns. Every name below has one trigger. Until it happens, leave him on waivers.

sections.heading: What to watch in weeks one and two

paragraphs.text: Coaches do odd things in the first two weeks. Watch for players getting unexpected minutes, new starters, depth chart changes and players being asked to do more. When a rotation change shows up, act quickly. A 28-minute starting role is the kind of signal that should get a bid.

Do not chase a hot shooting night, and do not drop a player after a cold one. If his role, minutes and usage are the same, nothing has changed. Base each add on the box score minutes, the starting lineup and the injury report.

The waiver wire matters as much as the draft in our league. We can make up to 6 adds per week and waivers run daily. Use those adds on players whose new role holds up, and on streamers who give extra games played in a head-to-head week.

sections.heading: New role or short injury: how much to bid

paragraphs.text: The notes point in two directions here. One side says to react fast. Grab hot players who stay hot, and move on new starters and bigger minutes before other managers do. The other side warns against boosting a fill-in starter much when the starter has a short injury. That injury may last only a few games, or none. Bench players who post big numbers during an injury should be valued close to their healthy-team role, which means around 150th unless something else changes.

Here is how we apply both views. Spend real FAB when the change is structural: a won starting job, a trade, or a clear jump in minutes with a healthy starter ahead of him. When the trigger is only an injury to the starter, bid small, use him as a short-term streamer and drop him when the starter returns. Precious Achiuwa is the clearest case. He is a backup center streamer only while Cardwell and Raynaud are out, and he should be dropped once both are back.

sections.heading: Starting jobs to check on opening night

paragraphs.text: The Lakers' wing spots are open. Jake LaRavia is worth keeping only if he is in the opening-night starting lineup. Matisse Thybulle needs to keep his starting job and play more than 22 minutes. Ziaire Williams needs to start and reach 30 minutes once his foot is fine.

Boston and Detroit have shooting guard and wing battles that matter for threes. Check whether Sam Hauser or Baylor Scheierman starts, and whether the starter plays more than about 23 to 25 minutes. In Detroit, Duncan Robinson needs to keep the starting shooting guard job, and Isaiah Joe becomes an add if he takes it from him.

Some center jobs are also undecided. Jalen Smith (Chicago), Hannes Steinbach (Charlotte), Mitchell Robinson (Boston) and Oso Ighodaro (Phoenix) each become quick FAB adds if they win the starting center job or the bigger share of minutes. For Robinson, the line is about 22 minutes. For Ighodaro, it is about 29.

Several guards and forwards need about 27 to 30 minutes to matter. Kris Dunn and De'Anthony Melton need to start at about 28 minutes. Keon Ellis needs the start over Mikel Brown Jr. and about 27 minutes. Jerami Grant needs to start over Wells at close to 30 minutes. Malik Monk needs about 27 minutes. Aaron Nesmith has top 100 upside if he keeps the start over Oubre and his FG% climbs back toward 48 to 50 percent.

sections.heading: Handcuffs: add the day the starter sits

paragraphs.text: Some backups only matter when one player is out. If that player misses time, they start. Joan Beringer for Gobert, Jock Landale for Okongwu, Isaiah Stewart for Edey, Andre Drummond for Towns, Marvin Bagley III for Jokic and Adem Bona for Embiid all fit this group. The notes project Beringer at 12 points, 10 rebounds and 2.4 blocks in starter minutes, and Landale at a 30-minute starter's role.

Guards work the same way. Tre Jones becomes an immediate add if Giddey or Powell is hurt or Powell is traded. Andrew Nembhard is an add if Haliburton's minutes are limited or he misses time. Collin Gillespie would start at about 30 minutes if Green, Booker, Brooks or Bridges gets hurt. A starting role would make Scotty Pippen Jr. a must add.

Keep the earlier rule in mind for all of these players. A fill-in start for a few games does not change a player's real value much. Bid to cover the missed games, not the season, unless the injury is long or a trade makes the role permanent.

Some players are useful for one category in the right week, not as roster fixtures. Alex Caruso streams for steals, best in punt PTS builds. T.J. McConnell streams for FG%, assists and steals in weeks when Indiana plays 4 games. Luke Kennard and Duncan Robinson stream for threes. Steven Adams streams for rebounds in good matchups. Each one uses up one of our 6 weekly adds, so pick him up for that week and drop him after.

Our playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, ending 2027-03-28. Phoenix, Memphis and Dallas play 4-4-4. The Clippers play 4-3-4 and New Orleans plays 4-4-3. The Lakers play only 3-4-3, Indiana plays 3-4-3, and Houston and Miami play 10 games total. Minnesota has a two-game week 20 and Cleveland a two-game finals week. Three of Boston's back-to-backs fall in our playoff weeks. When two waiver players have the same trigger, favor the one with the better playoff schedule.

Some names come later. Dereck Lively II is expected back around Thanksgiving and is a target only if he wins the starting job. Check Jimmy Butler III's return date and minutes around Christmas. Bradley Beal needs to get close to 30 minutes after he returns. Mikel Brown Jr., Josh Minott and Brayden Burries are second-half names if Brooklyn or Milwaukee pushes its young players, for example after the 2027-03-04 trade deadline.
